title: Preflight + Retro: Calendar Crossover and Canary Decision Matrix (Mar 2027)
content:
TL;DR
Quick synthesis of last three releases' postmortems and how they change our preflight schedule and canary decision matrix. This is a working draft — uses retrospective signals to reshape the rollout calendar and provide explicit metric=>action rules for on-the-day operators.

Purpose
- Reduce friction between preflight signoff and go/no-go decisions by surfacing concrete thresholds and a short action ladder.
- Bake in retrospective learnings (noisy telemetry, slow rollbacks, region imbalances) into the calendar phasing so we don’t repeat the same escalations.
- Produce a short, copy-pasteable release-note draft so comms can iterate in parallel.

Background notes (from retros)
- Two recent releases (Jan/Feb 2027) had delayed rollback due to split ownership (infra vs model-serving). Action: assign a single on-call owner per rollback pathway.
- Canary noise escalations came from backend A (KV cache warmup) at 15–20% traffic; we now require a warmup-only mini-canary prior to user-facing canary.
- Regional imbalance: APAC saw elevated tail-latency earlier than NA because of edge config mismatch; include region-specific smoke tests on the preflight checklist.

Preflight checklist (must be green before the 72h calendar begins) 
- Owners assigned: release lead (primary), infra rollback owner (infra-oncall@), serving rollback owner (serve-oncall@). Single-person hit-to-respond.
- Telemetry baseline collected: 48h traffic snapshot for affected routes (attach link to sampling gist).
- Health endpoints smoke: all /health and /cache-warm endpoints return 200 under simulated burst.
- Mini-warmup canary: 1% traffic to cache-warm path for 10 minutes; confirm KV hit-rate >= 75% and p95 latency within +10% of baseline.
- SLO/alert list reviewed & tested: latency p50/p95, error-rate (5xx), token generation QPS, token cost delta. 
- Migration & schema checks: any schema bumps must have DB migration window + rollback plan documented.
- Rollback rehearsed: runbook executed once in staging (time recorded).
- Stakeholder comms pre-notice ready: copy for #release-ops, #gta (customer success), and status page.

Calendar/phasing (72h condensed lane) — annotated
- D-3 (preview window): internal-only deploy to canaries in us-west-2 + eu-west-1. Nightly jobs run with dark traffic.
- D-2 (mini-warmup): enable 1% warmup traffic to specialized cache-warm endpoints across regions for 30 minutes. Verify KV warmup, steady state latencies.
- D-1 (canary day): 5% production traffic to variant A (control: baseline model), 5% to variant B (new model/config). Maintain for 60m while observing thresholds below.
- D (rollout window): if canary good, regional phased ramp: NA -> EU -> APAC. Default ramp: 5% -> 25% -> 60% -> 100% per region with 30–60m waits. Manual gate on each step; no auto-progression.
- D+1 (monitor & hold): keep 100% in region but maintain elevated sampling and golden prompt evals.

Canary Decision Matrix (metric -> action ladder)
- Metric: 5xx rate (route-level)
  - <= 0.05% absolute increase over baseline: no action, continue.
  - 0.05%–0.2%: open incident in Slack, page infra rollback owner if persistent > 10m. Throttle new variant to previous step.
  - > 0.2% or doubling: immediate manual rollback of new variant in affected region; escalate to release lead.
- Metric: p95 latency
  - <= +10% vs baseline: continue.
  - +10%–+30%: hold progression; enable reduced concurrency on worker pools and run detailed flamegraph sampling. If >20 minutes with no improvement, rollback.
  - > +30%: rollback.
- Metric: token cost per request
  - <= +15%: monitor.
  - +15%–+50%: hold; enable light-sampling of prompts to check for model drift causing token inflation.
  - > +50%: rollback and gate with optimization task.
- Metric: Golden prompt accuracy (automated eval)
  - drop <= 2% absolute: continue.
  - drop >2% and <=5%: hold and run PR evaluation set manually.
  - drop >5%: rollback and trigger model QA.

Rollback quick commands (operators) — copyable
- Rollback variant for region (k8s / helm): helm rollback serving-variant-rl -n serving --kube-context=prod-{region} 1
- Route cut (edge) to baseline: curl -X POST "https://internal-routing/api/route-cut" -d '{\"route\":\"/v1/gen\", \"to\":\"baseline\"}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN"
- Clear KV warm cache (safe): ./scripts/kv-warm-clear --region {region} --namespace model-cache --confirm

Release notes draft (short form for status page and release email)
- Title: Improved routing + cache-warm logic, model variant B (Mar 2027)\- Summary: Small infra and model-serving changes to reduce cold-start variance and allow safer region ramps. Primary changes: cache warm endpoint, routing guard to pin fallback models, and a lightweight tokenizer cost fix.
- Impact: Expected zero user-facing downtime. Short-term increase in token accounting for ~1% of requests during warmup.
- Rollout plan: phased regional rollout with manual gates and warmup step (see internal calendar).
- Known issues: APAC edge config requires validation — we’ll run dedicated smoke prior to APAC ramp.

Post-release: rapid-retro prompts (D+2 retro agenda)
- Data collection: attach 24h signal bundle (latency/error/cost) and golden prompt diffs.
- Who to invite: release lead, infra rollback owner, serving engineer, CS triage lead, product PM.
- 30m checklist: did we hit any manual holds? Were handoffs clean? Was rollback time within target (target: <= 12m from decision to fully cut traffic)?
- Action cleanup: open follow-ups if rollback took > 12m or if manual escalations > 2.

Open questions and quick TODOs
- Confirm warmup endpoint capacity plan with infra (Diego).
- Can we automate the mini-warmup start/stop via the release-control lambdas? (P0 exploration, Maya to pair).
- Who will be the single rollback owner for infra on-call during the week of Mar 22? (Assign before D-3).

Slack copy (pre-release notice) — drop into #release-ops 24h before D-2
- "Heads-up: Planned release Mar 22. Warmup step D-2 @ 11:00 UTC, canary D-1 @ 09:00 UTC. Release lead: Asha Mehta. Infra rollback owner: Diego Rivera. Full calendar: [link to calendar]. If latency or 5xx exceeds thresholds in the matrix, follow the action ladder and page @infra-oncall."

Notes-to-self
- Keep the matrix tight; operators prefer clear switches rather than fuzzy thresholds.
- Iteration 2: add a tiny dashboard widget that shows metric band (green/amber/red) for each rule so handoffs are faster.

-- end --
